summary: E2 tests whether a Go model can learn human moves and use player rank to adjust its play. This small trial did not show a benefit from rank input.
prompt: Choose the next step for E2 after inspecting the games. The model comparison is complete; data expansion and the readiness decision are still open.

readout.context: We trained two small Go models on the same 106 human games: one received player ranks and one did not. We compared both with KataGo Human SL, an existing model trained to predict human moves. Both test sets contain games excluded from training; one also uses a separate group of players.
results: Rank input did not improve the main move-prediction score in either test set. KataGo Human SL predicted human moves much better. These small, single-run results do not establish playing strength or human rank.
All 12 generated games replayed legally, but five endings could not be scored within the set checking budget. The learned models also passed too early in some positions.
The cached-data check found 295 extra training candidates. They still need legal replay and duplicate checks. Coverage is uneven, so more data may help but is not a promised fix.

review_steps.title: Read the short results above
review_steps.action: Check that the outcome and its limits are clear. Detailed scores are optional under Metrics; ask about anything unclear in your reply.
review_steps.why: This separates a working experiment from a model that is ready to use.

review_steps.title: Inspect one game from each model
review_steps.action: In Games, select each of the three models, click End, then use Before and After beside a pass. Note any odd ending or pass; include the game ID and move number. A spot check is enough for this handoff.
review_steps.why: Move prediction alone does not show whether a model finishes games sensibly.

review_steps.title: Choose the next E2 step
review_steps.action: In Next step, choose the cached-data build, broader data planning, or deferral. I recommend the cached-data build, capped at 6 CPU-hours and 8 elapsed hours, with no downloads or GPU work.
review_steps.why: It uses data already on disk to measure whether training coverage can improve before spending more on model training.

review_steps.title: Send back your choice and any findings
review_steps.action: Reply here, or use Export review notes and attach the saved JSON file. Include game IDs and move numbers for any concerns. Choosing an option in the page alone does not send it.
review_steps.why: Your response records the decision and tells us what to address before continuing.

limitations: Only one training run per model was compared. The two test sets contain 19 and 11 accounts, too few for a firm comparison at each rank.
Not every planned rank is represented. A rank supplied to the model is an input, not proof that it plays at that strength.
Only development data was evaluated. Data reserved for confirming results and for the final test stays untouched.
Each model played four games against simple opponents. This is too little evidence to approve a reliable training opponent or claim broad playing strength.
KataGo Human SL used its original move probabilities, fixed server-era/time settings, and full rules history. We do not know whether its training data overlaps these games.
Unknown results and missing judgments stay in the report. Extra moves used by the ending checker are not part of the model game or its training data.
GPU time includes loading, saving and idle time during each job. Some tracking-service CPU work is outside the measured boundary.
